column10: I, like many others, bought this product based on all the hype thinking it would be a miracle product for my skin. Basically what you are buying is a bottle of various essential oils, some added dyes (green and violet) and an undetermined percentage of trans retinol ester. Regardless of whether you love or hate this product, from a formulation standpoint it?™s pretty bad. They promote their use of trans retinol esters as a less irritating form of retinol, but then add a bunch of other ingredients known to be skin irritants that can cause you to develop sensitivity to them over time. It?™s pretty likely that if you are having a bad reaction to this product, it?™s due to the high percentage of fragrant essential oils and/or the added colorants. I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but the lovely blue color of this oil is not 100% natural. And while essential oils are great for their aromatherapy benefits, they need to stay out of skincare and go back to a diffuser. Essential oils are fragrant ingredients only and contain no known skincare benefits. So by continuing to put them on your face has the potential to do more harm than good because they are known skin irritants, especially at high concentrations which is the case with this product. If you are looking for a retinol treatment, or an oil, there are much better options. Don?™t let the pretty blue color fool you into believing this oil is worth the cost.

I believe this is called ?œdermaplaning.?œSounds strange, but I?™d recommend trying this if you have my type of skin and the same problem: (1) if you want to try dermaplaning like I did, do it at night BEFORE washing and treating your face (while skin?™s still dry, even if your makeup is still on because it helps you SEE where dead skin is soaking up color). column10: A few weeks ago, I was at the register of one of my favorite clothing stores and spied this gem sitting on the counter right next to the credit card machine. I have actually been anticipating this product?™s appearance on Sephora?™s website and know that I will not be the only one delighted to have this wonderful salve in a tube.Though I still carry both the new Rosebud Salve in a Tube and the originally Rosebud Salve in a Tin in my handbag (and even initially refused to take the tinned version out for fear of this new Rosebud Salve in a Tube being some wonky formula unlike the original), I found that I have not reached for the tinned one once since this purchase. Though both containers list the exact same ingredients in the exact same order, I am a paranoid person and was still concerned that something had been changed for better consistency in the tube. I do find the rosebud Salve in a Tube to go on more smoothly than the tinned salve but I am still not sure whether this is due to an actual change in texture/formula or just the vector by which I am applying The Salve. I think it may be due to the fact that this is far easier to apply to my lips than the tinned form and therefore I am using it more frequently. Also, I have not noticed any difference in quality, effectiveness, scent, or taste of The Salve.Also, though there is no difference in price between the tube and then tin, there is a rather large difference in quantity. column10: So, I never really write reviews for Sephora but have been in a deep search of skincare and understanding skincare regiment so I thought I would let other skincare junkies know about this mask and its versatility. Before I get into the actual product, I wanted to give an idea of how well this Vitamin C works within a skincare regimen that might have AHA/BHAs and/or Retinoids which are generally, no-no?™s for pairing with Vitamin C products. For my nightly routine, I usually double cleanse and then rotate days between an AHA (The Ordinary?™s Glycolic 7% Toner) and a Retinoid (The Ordinary?™s Granactive Retinoid 2% Emulsion. Now my original dilemma was that these are both ingredients that don?™t pair well with Vitamin C because of their ph levels. AHAs are usually higher in acidity (~3.0ish) and Retinoids are lower (at 4.5-5.5). Most Vitamin C products are L-Ascorbic Acid which is higher in acidity therefore making a retinoid useless and the vitamin c in turn, useless. HOWEVER, this miracle worker is actually a THD Ascorbate which means it is lower on the ph scale and can work well with a Retinoid and on days using an AHA, can be prepped by the Glycolic Acid Toner. I never in a million years though I would be one to know any of this, but I have been very meticulous about my skincare product ingredients lately so that I don?™t break out, become irritated, or over-exfoliate and damage my skin barrier. Moving on to the product, I bought this to replace the old (and better version) of the La Neige Water Bank Moisture Cream and I wasn?™t disappointed. This mask is a thicker consistency and a little definitely goes a long way which has justified its expense for me. Once you massage it into your skin, I will admit that it does sit at the surface longer than I?™d like, but a few minutes later and it?™s completely absorbed. I definitely love this mask and would say it is comparable to the Jet Lag Mask in terms of hydration. My best advice would be to try the mini and check it out!

For my nightly routine, I usually double cleanse and then rotate days between an AHA (The Ordinary?™s Glycolic 7% Toner) and a Retinoid (The Ordinary?™s Granactive Retinoid 2% Emulsion. I never in a million years though I would be one to know any of this, but I have been very meticulous about my skincare product ingredients lately so that I don?™t break out, become irritated, or over-exfoliate and damage my skin barrier.
